name: Pearson plc
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: regulated assessment and qualifications franchise (Pearson VUE test-delivery network, UK GCSE/A-level qualifications, PTE English test, clinical assessments) with institutional switching costs and trusted content/IP, but measured returns do not support a wide moat — fundamentals.json roic_proxy ran 3.0-9.3% over FY2019-FY2025 (7.7% in FY2025, best year 9.3% in FY2024) at a 47-52% gross margin (52.0% FY2025), i.e. around, not well above, the cost of capital through the cycle, while Higher Education courseware faces structural print/digital erosion and AI substitution pressure. Moat 5 gives CAP 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency GBP converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-13), Item 12, 'Description of securities other than equity securities — American Depositary Shares': 'Each ADS represents one ordinary share.' (sponsored ADR facility, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as depositary); the same statement appears in the business overview, and the cover page registers 'American Depositary Shares, each Representing One Ordinary Share, 25p per Ordinary Share'. The NYSE ADS facility is 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share.) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-13), consolidated cash flow statement: 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment and investment property' GBP 29M and 'Purchase of intangible assets' GBP 105M for FY2025 — total capex GBP 134M; the same statement reports GBP 33M + GBP 91M = GBP 124M for FY2024 and GBP 30M + GBP 96M = GBP 126M for FY2023. Declared in GBP (the reporting currency); the engine FX-converts at period-end ECB rates.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact — intangible purchases filed for FY2022 (90,000,000 GBP), FY2023 (96,000,000 GBP), FY2024 (91,000,000 GBP), FY2025 (105,000,000 GBP) were not added on top of the override; if the override excludes them, revise it to the total
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.5%) vs bull-case tier C (10.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Improving global education franchise with a regulated assessment moat, moat 5/10 — but at $18.19 it does not clear 15%: Tier D, weighted IRR 8.39%, weighted IV@15% $8.27; it clears the hurdle only below ~$8.27, less than half the current price.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Regulated assessment franchise — Pearson VUE global test-centre network and government/professional certification contracts are hard to replicate
Accredited qualifications with institutional lock-in — UK GCSE/A-levels, BTEC and PTE are embedded in school, university and immigration systems
Content and assessment IP plus data scale across 5 segments, 67% of sales in the US
Proven pricing power in assessments — FY2025 underlying sales +4% and H1 2026 +4% with adjusted operating margin expanding to 17.2%
moat_against: ROIC history is mediocre — roic_proxy 3.0-9.3% FY2019-FY2025, never durably above ~10%
Higher Education courseware in structural decline — print erosion, Inclusive Access price pressure, AI tools substituting for paid courseware and study help
Contract concentration and re-bid risk in assessments — US Student Assessment lost the New Jersey contract; government contracts re-tender
English Language Learning exposed to migration policy — H1 2026 ELL guidance cut on softer migration-driven demand; Duolingo-class consumer apps pressure the category
